scope: Twenty-ninth expansion batch, third mixed-context set:12 exercises in four send/borrow/wait/redo triplets. Current personal intention, absence of need and no available alternative share a three-way relationship. The whole ending is missing after a dictionary-form verb. The same pool and explicit basic-form restrictions apply throughout; this is bounded account selection, not unrestricted cloze or complete intention/outcome/necessity coverage.

sources.section: The Basics and Verb + tsumori: a speaker's intention and plain-form verbal attachment; short- and long-term plans. The current items give previously made personal decisions. Do not adopt categorical on-the-spot/third-person restrictions or universal failed-outcome and stronger-refusal interpretations from other parts of the page.

sources.publisher: The Japan Foundation, Nihongo Kokusai Center
sources.section: Koto part1, section3B item4: koto-wa-nai for unnecessary action, explicitly distinguished from negative experience or occasion; example20 explains that email or telephone removes the need for a special trip. Section3 subsection2A names desu, da and de-aru, supporting the copula distinction, not original-sentence attestation. Other broad koto/no substitution restrictions are outside this batch.

Actual meaning and attachment: suru-hitsuyou-wa-nai / shinai-hou-ga-ii, with V(dictionary) + koto-wa-nai. The text describes advice to a worried person and a possible critical use. This supports no-need overlap in the reassuring examples, not universal identity with prohibition or negative advice. The incorrect alternate URL in the search narrative was not used.

Actual Example B, Do not need to: kyou-wa-jimusho-ni-iku-hitsuyou-ga-nai, with the negative necessity explanation; Example C contrasts polite arimasen. Only the formation and no-need meaning are used. The later sample's supposed universal N3 employment requirement and exhaustive exam-marketing claims are not adopted.

Actual 必要 entry, reading hitsuyou, noun sense for need/requirement, and the separate returned 必要ない entry, reading hitsuyounai, expression/i-adjective meaning unnecessary/not needed. Recognizes the particleless form; it does not establish equal register, every original collocation or an obligatory spelling. The exercise format explicitly requests hiragana.

Actual usage and formation: unavailable alternatives with V(dictionary) + hoka-nai; shika-nai overlap; hoka-wa-nai as an alternate form. Its somewhat-formal tendency and possible resignation do not make either form a unique correct answer or require resentment. Sweeping claims in individual life/medical examples are not adopted.

Actual meaning, formation and taxi teaching sequence: V(dictionary) + shika-nai and V(dictionary) + optional yori before hoka; removing train and bus alternatives. The longer shikata-ga expansion lies outside the common basic-form instruction. Qualify its resignation emphasis using Hedgehog's possible, not obligatory, account; example-world claims are not generalized.

Actual About: no other available option after verbs, with optional ni, wa or ni-wa between hoka and nai. Combined with the inspected optional-yori formation and bare hoka evidence, this supports all eight hoka endings alongside shika-nai. No universal emphasis or register equality is claimed.

authoringNotes: All12 scenarios are original and require independent linguistic review, including all60 literal accepted endings:8 intention,16 no-need and36 no-alternative completions. The same four verbs occur in all three classes. Accepted equivalents share an identity and never appear as wrong buttons.

The common question-visible instruction names tsumori-da, koto-wa-nai, the three hitsuyou-nai/wa-nai/ga-nai forms, hoka-nai and shika-nai. It requests complete uncontracted plain nonpast hiragana endings, permits de-aru for tsumori and optional yori plus ni/wa/ni-wa for hoka, and excludes other added particles/auxiliary constructions. This is explicit basic-form practice, not a claim that unlisted no-need, decision, advice, negative-intention, polite or combined expressions are ungrammatical.

The full English meaning defines the intended account. A voluntary intention and absence of need can both be true: the optional extra mailing and redo deliberately establish this. Having a preferred route does not independently prove all other routes are unavailable, and a no-need statement does not prevent someone choosing the action. Do not infer intended behavior solely from a requirement or from its absence.

All plan items report current intentions based on prior personal choices. They do not claim the action is complete or guaranteed to succeed. The waiting plan concerns staying here, not denying that time must pass before the exhibition opens. Optionality for one requirement does not establish alternatives for a different chosen goal. Plan distractor feedback contrasts the requested intention with an unestablished sole-route claim; permission to abandon a goal is not another way to achieve it.

No-need examples give a satisfied application, supplied projector, server-side update and accepted program. Optional actions remain allowed. Koto-wa-nai can reassure or discourage an unnecessary effort; hitsuyou forms directly frame the need. The overlap is judged within these sentences, not as identical stance in every context. The particleless hitsuyou-nai is recognized without inferring frequency or sentence-level naturalness from a dictionary entry alone.

The nine no-alternative endings retain all reviewed hoka/shika variants. Necessity is relative to getting this application accepted, exhibiting here today, resuming this repair or submitting a qualifying copy. Giving up that goal or doing unrelated work can remain possible. The loan can be welcome; resignation is not mandatory, and having only one route does not guarantee successful completion.

The earlier plans, actions, hoka-exclusion and mixed-routine/time-state records and related article sections were screened. This adds intention-versus-practical-necessity selection and the hitsuyou no-need alternatives without revising older explicitly narrower tasks. Past intention/outcome, normative judgments and other mixed families are not declared complete.

All eight primary source pages were inspected. Bunpro's guessed hitsuyou-ga-aru URL returned404 and supplied no evidence; the actual JLPT Sensei page supplied the required negative example. Search prose contained mismatched question numbers/paths and unsupported register summaries; only actual passages at the URLs recorded here were used. The exact JMdict entries were read from the API response.

All365 earlier records and identities remain unchanged. Add one mixed intention/necessity article section and a reference bullet for the new necessity sources, plus README/contract scope and focused regressions. No Android, counter, schema, grading or SRS changes; broader mixed work remains open.
